Some patients have profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding. A defect in platelet aggregation has also been reported.

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) reported a Caucasian Italian girl (FS) who was the first child of nonconsanguineous parents. From the age of 5 years she had recurrent bleeding upper intestinal ulcers. She also had intestinal malrotation and partial duodenal intussusception. Ophthalmologic findings included dyschromatopsia, optic disc pallor, visual field defects, and optic neuropathy. At 22 years of age she had non-autoimmune diabetes mellitus and optic neuropathy, with preserved visual acuity and electrophysiologic tests and no optic atrophy. Other findings at that age were tinnitus due to bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss triggered by loud environments, entero-gastric bile reflux, slow intestinal transit, and bleeding upper intestinal ulcers. Her platelets showed a reduced and reversible aggregation defect in response to ADP, with absent platelet secretion in response to ADP. Aggregation in response to collagen was normal. Her parents and brother were heterozygous carriers. They had no ophthalmologic abnormalities, diabetes, or deafness, but they did have a reversible platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP.

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) pointed out that their patient had optic neuropathy rather than optic atrophy at age 22 years. They suggested that the 'asymptomatic' optic atrophy reported in Jordanian WFS2 patients may also have been optic neuropathy. Because optic atrophy is a main diagnostic criterion for Wolfram syndrome, they cautioned that the so-called WFS2 might not be a subtype of Wolfram syndrome. The Jordanian patients had been reported with a platelet aggregation defect in response to collagen, whereas their patient's defect was in response to ADP. Mozzillo et al. (2014) noted that aggregation to both agonists is calcium-mediated, and they proposed that different experimental conditions or variability between patients could explain the discrepancy.

paragraphs.text: Amr et al. (2007) studied 3 consanguineous families of Jordanian descent with Wolfram syndrome-2. In all 3 families they identified a single homozygous missense mutation in a novel, highly conserved zinc-finger gene, ZCD2 (CISD2). The mutation was a G-C transversion at nucleotide 109, predicting a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution. Amr et al. (2007) found that the mutation caused disease through aberrant splicing rather than through the amino acid change: it removed exon 2 from the mRNA and introduced a premature stop codon. They found no mutations in the WFS2 gene when they screened 377 probands with hearing loss.

paragraphs.text: In an Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome-2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) identified a homozygous intragenic deletion in the CISD2 gene affecting the whole of exon 2. Her parents and brother were heterozygous for the deletion. Mapping by SNP-array analysis restricted the maximum deletion size to a 2,050-bp region spanning from intron 2 to intron 3, with a minimum size of 739 bp. The deleted region included the codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain, which the authors suggested may result in a nonfunctional protein.

checks.evidence_quote: A G-->C transversion at nucleotide 109 predicts an amino acid change from glutamic acid to glutamine (E37Q).

checks.claim: The CISD2 c.109G-C mutation caused aberrant splicing, removing exon 2 from the mRNA and introducing a premature stop codon.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation was found to disrupt messenger RNA splicing by eliminating exon 2, and it results in the introduction of a premature stop codon.

checks.claim: Lymphoblastoid cells from Wolfram syndrome-2 patients homozygous for CISD2 c.109G-C showed a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium after thapsigargin stimulation than control cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Lymphoblastoid cells from affected individuals show a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium when stimulated with thapsigargin, compared with controls

paragraphs.text: In an Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome-2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) identified a homozygous intragenic deletion in the CISD2 gene affecting the whole of exon 2. Her parents and brother were heterozygous for the deletion and had a subclinical platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP. SNP-array analysis restricted the deletion to a maximum of 2,050 bp, spanning from intron 2 to intron 3, with a minimum size of 739 bp. The deleted region included the codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain.

checks.claim: In an Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome-2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) identified a homozygous intragenic deletion in the CISD2 gene affecting the whole of exon 2.
checks.evidence_quote: CISD2 cDNA sequencing revealed a novel homozygous deletion affecting the whole exon 2 of CISD2

checks.claim: The parents and brother of the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome-2 reported by Mozzillo et al. (2014) were heterozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: The deletion was homozygous in the proband and heterozygous in her parents and brother.

checks.claim: The parents and brother heterozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion had a subclinical platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP.
checks.evidence_quote: Her brother and parents carried the heterozygous mutation and were apparently healthy, although they showed subclinical defective platelet aggregation.
checks.explanation: The main text specifies that the defect was in response to ADP.

checks.claim: SNP-array analysis restricted the CISD2 exon 2 deletion to a maximum of 2,050 bp, spanning from intron 2 to intron 3.
checks.evidence_quote: Combining these data with the ones from PCR, we were able to map the proximal breakpoint
checks.explanation: The 2,050-bp maximum comes from combining SNP-array and PCR data, not from the SNP array alone (which gave 4,250 bp).

checks.claim: The minimum size of the CISD2 exon 2 deletion was 739 bp.
checks.evidence_quote: The minimum size of deletion was 739 bp while the maximum size was 4,250 bp.

checks.claim: The CISD2 exon 2 deletion region included the codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain.
checks.evidence_quote: the triplets coding for aminoacids WRSKT, from the position 102 to 106 of the polypeptide, are within the deleted region
checks.explanation: The domain spans amino acids 99 to 112.
